sentence: A 40-year-old man with a recent diagnosis of PNH was referred for renal evaluation.
In the previous 9 months he had had repeated episodes of dark urine and lower back pain.
He had severe hemolytic anemia, hemoglobin 7.7 mg/dl, undetectable haptoglobin, elevated LDH 3,800 U/l, requiring red blood cell transfusion.
Normal kidney function, creatinine 0.8 mg/dl, proteinuria of 427 mg/24 h, with albuminuria of 120 mg/24 h.
Hemoglobinuria with normal sediment, negative glycosuria, and normal fractional phosphate excretion.
In the subsequent 10 months he presented repeated hemolytic crises, with macroscopic hemoglobinuria.
He reported difficulty concentrating and recurrent headache.
An MRI showed marked signal hypointensity in the renal cortex in all sequences, and a brain MRI revealed multiple subcortical lacunar lesions.
Due to cerebral involvement attributable to PNH, treatment with eculizumab was initiated.
The patient progressed without new hemoglobinuria crises, with resolution of anemia and normalization of LDH (decreased haptoglobin persisting).
Seventeen months after the start of treatment, a repeat MRI showed normalization of the signal in the renal cortex.
Kidney function remained normal, with proteinuria 130 mg/day and negative hemoglobinuria.
